title: Fix the docs behind a misuse
prompt: Dispatchers complain that the app keeps interrupting them: six teams now open a blocking Dialog that says "Route saved!" after every save. You check the Dialog docs page. It opens with a live demo of exactly that success dialog, followed by a complete props table. There is no guidance on when to use Dialog versus Toast. Which changes would you make? Select all that apply.
hints: Remember which part of a page gets copied the most.
Good fixes act at the moment someone decides which component to use, inside the docs page itself.
explanation: The first example is the most-copied code on the page, so it was teaching the misuse; replacing it with a real blocking decision, like "Delete route?", changes what gets copied. A "when not to use" line and a do-and-don't pair name the exact mistake and point to Toast at the moment of decision. More props detail, a principles link, or answering teams one by one in Slack leave the page itself unchanged, so the next team repeats the mistake.

when-not.text: Add "When not to use: confirmations that don't need a decision. Use Toast instead." near the top of the page.
when-not.why: Correct. It names the misuse and the alternative where people decide.

props-detail.text: Expand the props table with more detail on the `open` and `onOpenChange` props.
props-detail.why: The props work fine; the teams chose the wrong component, which the props table can't address.

first-example.text: Replace the first example with a blocking decision such as "Delete route?" with Cancel and Delete actions.
first-example.why: Correct. The first example is what gets copied, so it must model the right use.

principles.text: Add a link to the design principles page at the top of the Dialog page.
principles.why: Principles are general; nobody follows a link to find out whether a save message should block the screen.

do-dont.text: Add a do-and-don't pair: Dialog for "Delete route?", Toast for "Route saved".
do-dont.why: Correct. Side-by-side examples make the boundary between the two components obvious at a glance.

slack.text: Reply to each of the six teams in Slack explaining the problem.
slack.why: It helps those six teams once, but the page still teaches the next team the same mistake.
